title: Exact geometric fibres and constructible detection for continuous normed-field coefficients
statement:
Let $F$ be a normed field with totally disconnected metric topology. On profinite sets put $C_F(P)=C(P,F)$, using all continuous functions [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]. For a scheme $Z$ put $F_Z=p_Z^*C_F$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use internal modules and their ordinary unbounded derived categories [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. For a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point] $x:\operatorname{Spec}k_x\to Z$, with $k_x$ algebraically closed, define
$$\Phi_{x,F}(M)=\Gamma((\operatorname{Spec}k_x)_{\mathrm{proet}},x^*M),$$
regarded as an abstract $F$-vector space through the constant sections. Here $x^*$ is the exact module inverse image with pulled-back coefficients [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Then $\Phi_{x,F}$ is an exact additive symmetric monoidal functor to $F$-vector spaces and sends $F_Z$ to $F$. Termwise application defines its t-exact functor on ordinary unbounded derived categories.

If $Z$ is Noetherian (quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]) and $M$ has finite constant local models on a finite constructible locally closed stratification [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model, def-constructible-stratification], then every $\Phi_{x,F}(M)$ is finite-dimensional. For morphisms between complexes with bounded cohomology of that kind, all the derived functors $\Phi_{x,F}$, as $x$ varies over geometric points, jointly reflect isomorphisms. This assertion of conservativity is restricted to these constructible complexes.

For a continuous field inclusion $F\hookrightarrow F'$ between totally disconnected normed fields, the fibres commute with exact scalar restriction. For every $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}_{F_Z})$ the specified canonical scalar/tensor comparison is an isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Vect}_{F'})$,
$$F'\otimes_F^{\mathbf L}\Phi_{x,F}(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Phi_{x,F'}(F'_Z\otimes_{F_Z}^{\mathbf L}K).$$
It is induced by the ordinary balanced map $a\otimes m\mapsto a\otimes m$ and preserves the insertion-of-one units. Completeness and flatness of the condensed field inclusion are not assumptions.

proof.text: Factor $x=i y$ through its stratum. The finite-model trivialization gives $y^*i^*M\cong F_s^r$ and sections $F^r$. Use $(iy)^*\cong y^*i^*$ to identify this with $x^*M$, proving finite dimensionality.

proof.text: Refine the two stratifications by fibre-product intersections. Pulling back the given local models and using $(gf)^*\cong f^*g^*$ retains finite models and identifies all refined geometric fibres with the original ones. The matrix test makes the map invertible on each stratum. Exact pullback kills its kernel and cokernel there; Noetherian stratum detection makes both zero on $Z$.

proof.text: If every derived fibre of $f:K\to L$ is invertible, step 2 makes every fibre of $H^qf$ invertible. Step 4 applies to the finite-model cohomology sheaves of source and target. Thus $H^qf$ is invertible for every $q$, so $f$ is invertible in the localization. No finite-model assertion about its cone is needed.

proof.text: The scalar-transport lemma gives exact restriction on $Z$ and its normalized fibre comparison. For extension use its internal/sectionwise equivalences and $\alpha_{x,F},\alpha_{x,F'}$ transports to apply K-flat scalar normalization to $x^{-1}$. Internal extension/inverse-image compatibility identifies the ordinary balancing map; the internal/sectionwise scalar-adjunction lemma also identifies its derived representatives and units. Compose this inverse-image comparison with the terminal derived scalar-sections isomorphism on $x^*K$. Both representative maps send $a\otimes m$ to $a\otimes m$, so the composite is the specified comparison and preserves $m\mapsto1\otimes m$, for all unbounded $K$.
